cells.rationale: Search summaries put the 10-year at 4.92% on 2026-11-02, after 4.94 on 2026-10-30 and 4.98 on 2026-10-29 (https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/dgs10), so the 4.94 threshold sits about 2 bp above the latest level and the yield has been drifting lower from a peak above 5.18% (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/02/treasury-yields-bonds-nonfarm-payrolls.html, 2026-10-02). A four-session move has a standard deviation of roughly 10-14 bp (an assumption, not a counted figure), which makes a 2 bp gap close to a coin flip, and a tie at 4.94 counts as No. Payrolls probably land on 2026-11-06 itself, which widens the spread of outcomes without tilting it, so I stay just under 50% with the weak, unchecked evidence.

note: Recorded before every entry's cutoff; scored as a separate method.
